newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC grants Questar Pipeline construction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC grants Questar Pipeline construction.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Tuesday granted a request from Questar Pipeline Co to build natural gas pipeline-looping facilities in Wyoming and Utah to expand capacity, subject to several environmental conditions.

The project is to increase Questar's transmission system capacity on the critical connecting link between its southern and northern mainlines, and will be built between Questar's Clay Basin underground gas storage field and the Nighteningale/Kanda/Coleman Compressor Complex.
Questar, which said it has several firm commitments for transportation for the project, plans to build the 41.2 miles of 20-inch pipeline in two phases.
The first phase pipeline loop would extend 27.6 miles north from Clay Basin at a cost of about $11.55 million, and the second phase would extend 13.6 miles and would cost about $6.276 million.
Questar requested that the construction costs qualify for predetermined rolled-in rate treatment.
The company said the net rate impact from rolling either the project's costs into the current rate design would be below the the 5 percent threshold for a presumption of rolled-in rate treatment.
